source: NCERT Class VI, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Many Names, One Land
points: The subcontinent has been known by several names across time: **Bharat, Bharatavarsha, Jambudvipa, Aryavarta, Hind, Hindustan** and **India**.
Each name arose in a different language or period, but all point to the same civilisational land.
The Constitution of India (**Article 1**) opens: **"India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States."**

sections.heading: 2. Bharata and Bharatavarsha
points: **Bharata** is an ancient name found in Indian texts; **Bharatavarsha** means "the land (varsha) of Bharata."
Traditions link the name to legendary figures named Bharata — including the son of **Rishabha** (Jain tradition) and, in the epics, the son of **Dushyanta and Shakuntala**.
The **Bharatas** were also an important people (jana) mentioned in the **Rigveda**.
**varsha** = a region/land in ancient geography.

sections.heading: 3. Jambudvipa and Sapta-Sindhu
points: **Jambudvipa** = "the island/land of the **jambu** (rose-apple) tree" — an ancient name for the subcontinent used in the **Puranas** and in **Ashoka's inscriptions**.
**Sapta-Sindhu** = "the land of **seven rivers**" — a Rigvedic name for the north-western region.
**dvipa** = island/landmass; **Sindhu** = river (especially the Indus).

sections.heading: 4. From Sindhu to Hind and India
points: The **Sindhu (Indus)** river gave the land its outward-facing names.
**Persians** pronounced *Sindhu* as **Hindu** → the land became **Hind / Hindustan**.
**Greeks** wrote it as **Indos** → **India**.
**Arabs** called it **Al-Hind**.
So "Hindu," "Hind" and "India" all trace back to the river **Sindhu**, not originally to any religion.

sections.heading: 5. Aryavarta and Other Names
points: **Aryavarta** = "land of the **aryas** (noble/cultured people)" — used for the northern plains.
**Meluhha** — the name by which **Mesopotamians** referred to the Harappan/Indus region.
Names reflect how a land is seen from within (Bharata, Jambudvipa) and from outside (Hind, India, Meluhha).

sections.heading: 6. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Bharatavarsha = "land of Bharata"; Bharatas = a Rigvedic people.
Jambudvipa = land of the rose-apple (jambu) tree; used in Ashoka's inscriptions.
Sapta-Sindhu = land of seven rivers (Rigveda).
Sindhu → (Persian) Hindu → Hind/Hindustan; (Greek) Indos → India; (Arabic) Al-Hind.
Aryavarta = land of the aryas; Meluhha = Mesopotamian name for the Indus region.
Constitution, Article 1: "India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States."

sections.heading: 7. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: "Hindu/Hind" originally derives from the **river Sindhu**, a geographical name — not a religious one.
**Jambudvipa** = rose-apple (jambu) tree, not any other plant.
**Meluhha** was the **Mesopotamian** name for the Indus region (do not confuse with Dilmun = Bahrain, Magan = Oman).
The "India, that is Bharat" wording is from **Article 1** of the Constitution.
